intro: Dagmar Cannabis' West Broadway store is at 412 West Broadway in SoHo, between Prince and Spring, in the heart of the gallery and boutique blocks. It is the smallest of the four licensed dispensaries we track in SoHo, with about 190 products from 38 brands. Pre-rolls are the clear focus at 82 listings, followed by 58 edibles, 23 flower options and 18 vapes, with seven concentrates.

Ayrloom leads the brand list at 17 products, and Heady Tree, Wyld, Camino, Stone Road and Nanticoke each have around ten, a mix that favors New York pre-roll makers and name-brand gummies. The entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom's 2:1 drinks in yuzu citrus, cranberry apple, black cherry and half-and-half. Dagmar also runs stores in the West Village and Williamsburg. For vapes or flower, Alta on Kenmare and The Travel Agency on Broadway both list far more; this is the stop for a quick pre-roll or gummy on West Broadway.
know: About 190 products from 38 brands; pre-rolls (82) make up more than 40 percent of the menu.
Heady Tree, Stone Road and Nanticoke supply the pre-roll depth; Wyld and Camino cover gummies.
Entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom 2:1 drinks.
One of three Dagmar stores; Alta and The Travel Agency are larger SoHo alternatives.

faq.q: What does Dagmar West Broadway specialize in?
faq.a: Pre-rolls. With 82 of its 190 listings being joints, from Heady Tree, Stone Road, Nanticoke and others, it has more pre-roll variety than its size suggests. Vapes and flower are thin at 18 and 23.

faq.q: Is this the same as Dagmar in the West Village?
faq.a: Same operator, different store. Dagmar runs licensed shops on West Broadway in SoHo, Jane Street in the West Village and North 11th Street in Williamsburg. Each menu is small and pre-roll heavy, with Ruby Farms deeper at the other two.

faq.q: Can I consume on West Broadway after buying?
faq.a: Smoking is allowed on public sidewalks where tobacco smoking is allowed, but not inside the store, in parks or near building entrances. Many people choose drinks or gummies to avoid the question in a busy shopping district.

intro: Nicklz is at 797 8th Avenue in Midtown, near 48th Street on the west side of the Theater District, a few blocks from Times Square and the 50th Street C and E station. It is the smallest of the seven licensed dispensaries we track in Midtown, with about 190 products from 41 brands. Edibles dominate at 76 listings, followed by 38 vapes, 32 pre-rolls and 28 flower options, plus an 11-item concentrate case.

MFNY and 1906 are the deepest brands at 15 and 14 products, with NYCE, Rove, Camino and Off Hours behind them. The entry price is $5 for 1906's drop pouches in Genius, Boost, Go and Bliss, each a one- or two-dose sampler. For theatergoers and anyone staying in the hotel blocks west of Broadway, Nicklz is the closest licensed shop; for a full selection, Qube on Broadway at 39th Street lists more than ten times as many products about a ten-minute walk south.
know: About 190 products from 41 brands; edibles (76) are 40 percent of the menu.
MFNY and 1906 lead the brand list; 11 concentrates is a solid case for the size.
Entry price is $5 for 1906 drop pouches in four formulas.
Closest licensed dispensary to the Theater District's west side; Qube is the larger Midtown option.

faq.q: Is Nicklz near Times Square?
faq.a: Yes. It is on 8th Avenue at 48th Street, about a five-minute walk west of Times Square and close to the Theater District hotels. The 50th Street C and E station is two blocks north.

faq.q: What is the cheapest thing at Nicklz?
faq.a: 1906 drop pouches at $5 before tax, in Genius, Boost, Go and Bliss. They are low-dose swallowable drops, between 2.5 and five milligrams per piece, so a pouch is a gentle introduction.

faq.q: Does Nicklz have a good concentrate selection?
faq.a: For its size, yes. Eleven listings, with MFNY supplying live resin. Qube and Culture House carry larger cases if you want more choice.

intro: Dagmar Cannabis' Williamsburg store is at 61 North 11th Street, between Wythe and Kent, a block from the waterfront and a short walk from the Bedford Avenue L. It is the fifth-largest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in Williamsburg, with about 185 products from 34 brands. Pre-rolls make up nearly half the menu at 84 listings, followed by 49 edibles, 30 vapes and just 11 flower options, with eight concentrates.

Ruby Farms is the deepest brand at 21 products, and Ayrloom, MFNY, Dank By Definition, Grön and Toast follow. That makes it a reliable stop for Ruby Farms' New York-grown pre-rolls in particular. The entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom's half-and-half, Honeycrisp and lemonade drinks and Harney Brothers' orange mango seltzer. Gotham's Domino store a few blocks south lists almost three times as many products, so Dagmar is the quick north-side stop rather than a destination.
know: About 185 products from 34 brands; pre-rolls (84) are nearly half the menu.
Ruby Farms leads at 21 products, with Dank By Definition adding more New York pre-rolls.
Entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom and Harney Brothers drinks.
Gotham Domino, a few blocks south, is the larger licensed option on the waterfront.

faq.q: Is Dagmar Williamsburg good for pre-rolls?
faq.a: Yes. Pre-rolls are 84 of its 185 listings, and Ruby Farms, the most-stocked pre-roll brand in New York, is its deepest line at 21 products. Dank By Definition adds another ten.

faq.q: Does it carry flower?
faq.a: Very little, 11 listings. If you want loose flower in north Williamsburg, Gotham Domino and Twisted Vibrations on Broadway both have more.

faq.q: Where is it relative to the Bedford L?
faq.a: About a five-minute walk west along North 7th or North 11th toward the river. The shop is between Wythe and Kent, near the Wythe Hotel and Brooklyn Bowl.

intro: Dagmar Cannabis' West Village store is at 66 Jane Street, between Greenwich and Washington Streets, two blocks from the Hudson and a short walk from the 14th Street A, C, E and L station. It is one of the smaller licensed dispensaries we track across the East and West Village, with about 175 products from 31 brands. Pre-rolls lead at 77 listings, followed by 36 edibles, 31 flower options and 25 vapes. There are no concentrates listed.

Ruby Farms is the standout brand at 29 products, the deepest run of that label at any Village shop, with Ayrloom at 17 and Revert Cannabis, Camino, Off Hours and Milkweed behind. The entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom's 2:1 drinks in half-and-half, Honeycrisp, black cherry and lemonade. The Flowery on Christopher Street, about five minutes south, lists nearly three times as many products; Dagmar Jane Street is the pick for the far west side and for anyone who buys Ruby Farms.
know: About 175 products from 31 brands; pre-rolls (77) are 44 percent of the menu.
29 Ruby Farms products, the deepest run of that brand in the Village.
Entry price is $5.50 for Ayrloom 2:1 drinks; no concentrates listed.
The Flowery West Village on Christopher Street is the larger nearby option.

faq.q: Why shop at Dagmar West Village over The Flowery?
faq.a: Location and Ruby Farms. It is the westernmost licensed shop in the Village, close to the Whitney and the Hudson River Park, and it stocks 29 Ruby Farms products, more than The Flowery. For overall selection, The Flowery wins.

faq.q: Does Dagmar West Village have concentrates?
faq.a: No concentrates are listed. The menu is pre-rolls, edibles, flower and vapes, with a few tinctures and a topical.

faq.q: Is it close to the Meatpacking District?
faq.a: Yes. Jane Street is one block south of the Meatpacking District, a few minutes from the Whitney Museum and the southern end of the High Line.

intro: Smacked's Bleecker Street store is at 144 Bleecker, between LaGuardia Place and Thompson Street, in the middle of the Greenwich Village music and bar strip near NYU. It is one of the smaller licensed dispensaries we track in the East and West Village, with about 155 products from 27 brands. Vapes lead at 50 listings, with 45 edibles, 30 pre-rolls and 24 flower options, plus six concentrates.

Plug Play is the deepest brand at 11 products, giving the shop a pod-vape identity, with MFNY, Rove, 1906, Heady Tree and Off Hours behind it. The entry price is $6 for Layup drinks in limeade, futbol punch, peach tea and raspberry tea. Smacked was one of the first licensed dispensaries to open in New York, originally on Bleecker Street as a pop-up before settling in. For a wider selection, The Flowery's stores on Christopher Street and 1st Avenue each list roughly three times as many products.
know: About 155 products from 27 brands; vapes (50) are the largest category.
Plug Play pod vapes are the deepest line at 11 products; Rove and MFNY add cartridges.
Entry price is $6 for Layup beverages.
One of New York's earliest licensed shops; The Flowery West Village is the larger nearby menu.

faq.q: What is Plug Play?
faq.a: A pod-based vape system where a battery accepts proprietary pods. Smacked stocks 11 Plug Play products, the deepest selection of that brand among the Village shops we track, alongside standard 510 cartridges from Rove and MFNY.

faq.q: Is Smacked near NYU?
faq.a: Yes. It is on Bleecker between LaGuardia and Thompson, about two blocks south of Washington Square Park. NYU students must still be 21 or older with valid ID to enter.

faq.q: Does Smacked carry flower?
faq.a: A small selection, 24 listings. The menu is weighted toward vapes and edibles. For flower in the Village, The Flowery's two stores and PRYZM on Avenue A have more.

intro: Smiley Exotics is at 201 East 30th Street in Kips Bay, near 3rd Avenue and a short walk from the 28th Street 6 station. We group it with Gramercy and Union Square, where it is the smallest of three licensed dispensaries we track, with about 150 products from 35 brands. The menu is evenly spread: 40 vapes, 38 edibles, 32 pre-rolls and 27 flower options, plus eight concentrates and six tinctures.

Ayrloom is the deepest brand at 26 products, which is unusually concentrated for a shop this size, with Ruby Farms at 14 and Off Hours, Nanticoke, BLOOM and Mfused behind. The entry price is $5.65 for Ayrloom drinks in root beer, vanilla cola, yuzu citrus and cranberry apple. Green Genius on 3rd Avenue at 19th Street lists more than three times as many products; Smiley is the closer licensed shop for Kips Bay, Murray Hill and the NYU Langone blocks.
know: About 150 products from 35 brands, balanced across vapes, edibles, pre-rolls and flower.
Ayrloom makes up 26 listings, about a sixth of the whole menu.
Entry price is $5.65 for Ayrloom 2:1 drinks.
Green Genius, eleven blocks south on 3rd Avenue, is the larger nearby alternative.

faq.q: Is Smiley Exotics the only dispensary in Kips Bay?
faq.a: It is the only licensed one we track between 23rd and 34th Streets on the east side. Green Genius at 19th Street and Bud & Honey on 5th Avenue at 27th are the nearest others.

faq.q: What does Smiley carry from Ayrloom?
faq.a: Twenty-six Ayrloom products, covering the brand's drinks, gummies, vapes, tinctures and topicals. Ayrloom is a New York producer from the Beak & Skiff orchard family in central New York, and this is one of the fuller runs of its line in Manhattan.

faq.q: Do I need to be a New York resident?
faq.a: No. Any adult 21 or older with a valid government photo ID can shop at a licensed New York dispensary. Out-of-state and international IDs are accepted.

intro: Twisted Vibrations is at 301 Broadway in south Williamsburg, near Marcy Avenue and a block from the Marcy Avenue J, M and Z station. It is the smallest of the six licensed dispensaries we track in Williamsburg, with about 135 products from 44 brands. Flower is the biggest category at 41 listings, followed by 35 vapes, 23 pre-rolls and 22 edibles, with eight concentrates.

The brand list is more eclectic than the stock size suggests. STIIIZY is the deepest at 15 products, and Hurley, EUREKA, nama, Boukét and Ithaca Cultivated follow, which adds a couple of upstate New York growers you will not find at every shop. The entry price is $5.65 for Ayrloom singles in half-and-half iced tea lemonade, Honeycrisp cider, lemonade and rosé. For a bigger menu, Gotham Domino and The Flowery Brooklyn are each about 15 minutes north; Twisted Vibrations is the licensed option for south Williamsburg and the Broadway corridor.
know: About 135 products from 44 brands; flower (41) is the largest category.
STIIIZY leads at 15 products; Hurley, Boukét and Ithaca Cultivated add New York flower.
Entry price is $5.65 for Ayrloom single-serve drinks.
Only licensed dispensary we track in south Williamsburg; a block from the Marcy Avenue J, M and Z.

faq.q: Is Twisted Vibrations a flower shop?
faq.a: More than most. Flower is its largest category at 41 of 135 listings, with Hurley, Boukét and Ithaca Cultivated among the New York growers stocked. That ratio is higher than any other Williamsburg dispensary we track.

faq.q: Which train is closest?
faq.a: The Marcy Avenue J, M and Z station is a block away on Broadway. It is also a short walk from the Brooklyn side of the Williamsburg Bridge.

faq.q: How does it compare to Gotham Domino?
faq.a: Gotham Domino lists about 515 products to Twisted Vibrations' 135. Twisted Vibrations wins on proximity for south Williamsburg and on a few upstate flower brands; Gotham has the broader menu.

intro: Astoria Bud Boutique is at 30-12 Astoria Boulevard, near 31st Street and a block from the Astoria Boulevard N and W station. It is the smallest of the three licensed dispensaries we track in Astoria, with about 115 products from 33 brands. Pre-rolls lead at 36 listings, with 30 flower options, 27 edibles and 18 vapes, plus three concentrates.

Boukét, a New York flower brand, is the deepest line at 15 products, with Jaunty at 12 and Heavy Hitters, nama, Rolling Green Cannabis and Birdies behind. The entry price is $5.20 for Weed Water's P.O.G. Wowie and yuzu peach cans, with nama Relax Plus gummies and Cycling Frog black currant seltzer at $5.65. Terp Bros on Steinway and Cannavita on Ditmars both list several hundred more products, so Astoria Bud Boutique is the quick stop by the N and W, strongest for Boukét flower.
know: About 115 products from 33 brands; pre-rolls (36) and flower (30) lead.
Boukét flower is the deepest line at 15 products; Jaunty covers vapes.
Entry price is $5.20 for Weed Water cans.
Terp Bros and Cannavita, both in Astoria, carry far larger menus.

faq.q: Which Astoria dispensary is biggest?
faq.a: Terp Bros on Steinway Street, with about 800 products, then Cannavita on Ditmars with about 730. Astoria Bud Boutique is the smallest at about 115, but it is the closest to the Astoria Boulevard N and W station.

faq.q: What is Boukét?
faq.a: A New York cannabis brand focused on flower and pre-rolls. Astoria Bud Boutique lists 15 Boukét products, about half of its flower and pre-roll selection combined.

faq.q: Is it near the Triborough Bridge?
faq.a: Yes. Astoria Boulevard at 31st Street is a few blocks from the RFK Bridge approach and the Grand Central Parkway, which makes it a practical stop for drivers as well as N and W riders.

intro: By Any Other Name is at 946 Fulton Street in Clinton Hill, near Grand Avenue and a short walk from the Clinton-Washington Avenues C and G stations. It is the only licensed dispensary we track in Clinton Hill, with about 100 products from 30 brands. Flower is the biggest category at 40 listings, followed by 26 vapes and 19 pre-rolls. Edibles are a thin eight, and there are seven concentrates.

Hepworth and Aeterna tie as the deepest brands at 12 products each, both New York growers, with Grams, Ayrloom, Stranman and dompen behind. That gives the shop a flower-first identity that is rare at this size. The entry price is $6 for Ayrloom drinks in Honeycrisp 1:1, root beer, lemonade and cranberry apple. For edibles or a larger menu, Happy Buds in Bed-Stuy and The Travel Agency in Downtown Brooklyn are each about 15 minutes away by bus or bike.
know: About 100 products from 30 brands; flower (40) is the largest category.
Hepworth and Aeterna, both New York growers, lead at 12 products each.
Entry price is $6 for Ayrloom drinks; edibles are limited to eight listings.
Only licensed dispensary we track in Clinton Hill, near the Clinton-Washington C and G.

faq.q: What does By Any Other Name do best?
faq.a: New York flower. With Hepworth and Aeterna as its deepest brands and 40 flower listings out of about 100 products, it has a higher share of loose flower than almost any shop we track.

faq.q: Does it have many edibles?
faq.a: No, only eight listings. For gummies or drinks nearby, Happy Buds in Bed-Stuy or Be. in Park Slope carry much more.

faq.q: Is Clinton Hill near Fort Greene?
faq.a: Yes. Fulton Street at Grand Avenue is a few blocks east of Fort Greene Park and about a ten-minute walk from the Brooklyn Academy of Music, with no licensed dispensary in Fort Greene itself.

intro: Sky High Club is at 129 Loisaida Avenue in the East Village, which is Avenue C near 8th Street, deep in Alphabet City. It is the smallest licensed dispensary we track in the East and West Village, with about 70 products from 26 brands. Flower leads at 24 listings, followed by 15 edibles, 14 pre-rolls and 12 vapes, with three concentrates.

BLOOM and Off Hours are the deepest brands at six products each, with Cheech & Chong, BudJet, nama and Eaton Botanicals behind. The entry price is $15 for single pre-rolls from Road Trip, Cheech & Chong, BudJet and Sunday, including a Blue Dream and a Lemon Cherry Gelato. There are no $5 drinks or low-dose tablets listed. PRYZM on Avenue A and Gotham on the Bowery each carry about seven times as many products within a ten-minute walk, so Sky High Club is the convenient option for the far east side of the neighborhood.
know: About 70 products from 26 brands; flower (24) is the largest category.
Cheech & Chong and BudJet pre-rolls are among the more distinctive lines stocked.
Entry price is $15 for a single pre-roll; no sub-$10 items listed.
PRYZM on Avenue A is the nearest larger licensed menu.

faq.q: Where exactly is Loisaida Avenue?
faq.a: Loisaida Avenue is the co-name for Avenue C in the East Village. The shop is near 8th Street, a few blocks east of Tompkins Square Park and the Avenue A shops.

faq.q: Why is the cheapest item $15?
faq.a: Sky High Club does not list the $5 single-serve drinks or low-dose tablets that set the floor at most licensed shops. Its lowest-priced items are single pre-rolls at $15 before tax.

faq.q: What should I expect from a 70-product menu?
faq.a: A curated rather than comprehensive shop. Flower is the best-covered category, and brands like Cheech & Chong and BudJet give it a few options other Village shops do not carry. For breadth, PRYZM and Gotham Bowery are close.

intro: Bud City Cannabis is at 3343 Fulton Street in East New York, near Crescent Street and a short walk from the Crescent Street J and Z station on the Brooklyn and Queens border. It is the only licensed dispensary we track in East New York, and at the time of our last menu pull it listed just nine products from four brands, by far the smallest licensed menu in our data. Five of those are flower, with one each of edibles, topicals, vapes and concentrates.

Dumbo Electric supplies three of the nine products, MFNY two, and 1906 and Ayrloom one apiece. The entry price is $22.50 for a Tropicana Cherry flower listing, with a 1906 Bliss tin at $32.12, an MFNY Chemdog live resin cartridge at $45 and an Ayrloom Revive topical at $55. A menu this small usually means the shop is newly opened or publishes only part of its stock online, so it is worth checking the store's own menu or calling before a trip. The nearest larger licensed shops are Happy Buds in Bed-Stuy and Stash Master in Bushwick.
know: Nine products from four brands at our last pull, the smallest licensed menu we track.
Five flower listings, plus one edible, one topical, one vape and one concentrate.
Entry price is $22.50 for Tropicana Cherry flower.
Only licensed dispensary we track in East New York; Happy Buds and Stash Master are the nearest larger menus.

faq.q: Why does Bud City have so few products listed?
faq.a: Nine products is far below the 300 to 500 typical of a licensed New York shop. The likeliest explanations are a recent opening or an online menu that does not reflect the full counter. Confirm with the store directly before making a trip for a specific item.

faq.q: Is Bud City licensed?
faq.a: Yes. Sensei lists only dispensaries licensed by New York's Office of Cannabis Management. The small menu reflects what the shop publishes, not its license status.

faq.q: What is nearby if Bud City doesn't have what I want?
faq.a: Happy Buds in Bed-Stuy, with about 370 products, and Stash Master in Bushwick, with more than 1,100, are the nearest licensed shops with full menus. Both are reachable by the J or the A and C lines.
